constraints.text: The grace is at least the longest life of a quote, so no honest quote dies at a rotation ({11 §4.7}, KR-3).
The grace is at most twice the longest life of a quote, so a retired key does not linger ({11 §4.7}, KR-3).
The security notice is never longer than the standard notice.
Customers have at least as long after a sunset to recover as they had before it to prepare.
One mandate with the maximum number of tokens must fit in the exposure index.
The exposure bound does not exceed the token slots of one batch.
The timelock delay is at least 24 hours.
The recipient-change delay is at least 48 hours (OD-022).
The three window lengths are exactly these numbers of seconds.
The window lengths are whole multiples of the day.
A migration needs the successor and the predecessor to be live together ({12 §3}).
The ceiling admits the default quote TTL of 120 seconds (OD-027; backend-tunable, not a record).

Gas of a plan step: `MAX_BATCH` entries of `MAX_TOKENS_PER_MANDATE` tokens each (containment, exposure updates, Permit2 reads) must fit half of the per-transaction gas cap of the launch chains. Measured on the contracts at the EVM schedule of the compiler's target: about 6.5 million gas at the proposal (10), about 30 million at the earlier 50; not measured on the chains (RP-19).

Replacement cadence: `MIN_NOTICE_STANDARD` and `MAX_ROUTERS_LIVE` together bound how often a router can be replaced; with two live routers a third cannot be activated until the deprecated one is SUNSET, at least `MIN_NOTICE_STANDARD` after its deprecation.

Recovery latency: after emergency removals empty the current quote signer set, fiat-capped charges fail closed until governance's replacement set passes the timelock; `TIMELOCK_MIN_DELAY` is that latency ({11 §4.7}, KR-9).
The blast radius B2 depends on both ceilings: `MAX_BAND_WIDTH_BPS` bounds how far a signer can mis-price and `MAX_QUOTE_TTL` for how long ({11 §6}).
One text, one hash: the `AccountPin` string is identical in {12 §5.3} and {17 §5.1} and equals what PC-09 fixes; `PIN_EOA` is a hash tag (PC-09) and the pin sentinel (PC-15).
Identifier chain: `LINEAGE_TAG`, `MANDATE_TAG` and `CYCLE_TAG` (PC-09) and the cycle rule (PC-16) together define the settle-once identity; a change to one changes `cycleId` and `paymentId`.
Window grid: `DAY`, `WEEK` and `THIRTY_DAYS` (PC-10) are the grids of the lineage counters and `periodSeconds` is lineage data; the cycle rule (PC-16) divides by `periodSeconds`.
Fee ceiling: bounds every mandate's `maxFeeBps` ({11 §3}, clause K.8 of {12 §5.3.2}) and `setFee`; no numeric constraint can be stated until Finance decides (OD-016).
Permit2: one address per chain; the masked code hash is chain-independent and the two immutables (chain id at byte 6945, domain separator at byte 6983) differ per chain.
The guardian's power set is a subset of the guardian row of the authority matrix ({04 §5}): it stops, never resumes or widens; everything it cannot do waits for the timelock.
A recipient change is two-party and, if high-risk, sets new charges to `PAUSED_BY_RISK` (OD-022); the delay applies to every change.

records.name: MIN_NOTICE_STANDARD: minimum notice before a standard router sunset
records.enforcedIn: `RouterRegistry`: `deprecate` requires `sunsetNotBefore >= now + MIN_NOTICE_STANDARD`; `extendSunset` accepts later dates only; invariant `I-MIG-6` ({12 §3}, {12 §13}, {16 §8.1})

testnet.text: 20 minutes (1,200 s) in a `-testconst` build; the guard logic is identical ({16 §6}); rule T-3 requires one fork run at 180 days with a time warp before the audit starts

rationale.why: Sunset cannot happen before `deprecation + MIN_NOTICE_STANDARD`, and governance can lengthen the notice but never shorten it ({12 §3}). 180 days gives the customer-communication timeline of {12 §11.1} room to run in full: the announcement at the start, reminders at 150, 120 and 90 days before sunset, a second-level reminder at 60 days, urgent reminders from 30 days. ASM-028 assumes that with 180 days at least 90% of active mandates migrate before sunset; that assumption is untested.
rationale.prevents: A value that is too short strands customers who cannot or will not act in time: their mandates become `MIGRATION_REQUIRED` and stop charging (RISK-026). A value that is too long delays routine retirement and, together with `MAX_ROUTERS_LIVE` (PC-12), limits how often a router can be replaced.
rationale.mine: The value 180 days is the `PROPOSAL` of {12 §13} and OD-026; it is not a decision. The hard minimum (150 days, the first reminder of the {12 §11.1} schedule), the hard maximum (365 days) and the statement that a standard replacement needs one notice period each are my proposals for the approvers to confirm or change.

records.name: MIN_NOTICE_SECURITY: minimum notice before a security-driven router sunset
records.enforcedIn: `RouterRegistry`: `deprecate` with reason `SECURITY` requires `sunsetNotBefore >= now + MIN_NOTICE_SECURITY` and a security-notice hash; invariant `I-MIG-6` ({12 §3}, {12 §13})

rationale.why: The security path inside the immutable lifecycle: a router that is unsafe but not so urgent that the guardian disables it still has to give customers time to migrate. 60 days is the proposal of OD-026. The compressed timeline of {12 §11.1} (announcement, three days later, then 30, 14, 7, 3 and 1 days before sunset) fits inside it. Since 0.5 a `SECURITY` deprecation puts the router in emergency mode ({12 §5.3.1}), so customers who migrate must lock down every exposed token and their sibling mandates stop until their own successors exist; the notice has to be long enough to do that for every lineage.
rationale.prevents: Too short: customers cannot complete a three-step migration before sunset, unmigrated mandates go to `MIGRATION_REQUIRED`, and a short deadline is the pretext a phishing campaign would imitate (RISK-026). Too long: a router that FastPay itself has declared unsafe keeps charging for the whole notice; the immediate path for a real emergency is the guardian's stop, not this constant.
rationale.mine: 60 days is the proposal of OD-026, not a decision. My additions: the hard minimum of 45 days (the compressed timeline needs more than 33 days because the message three days after the announcement must come before the one 30 days before sunset; 45 leaves about 12 days of margin) and the hard maximum equal to PC-01 (a security notice longer than the standard one makes no sense).

records.name: RETENTION: minimum time a router stays SUNSET before it can be RETIRED
records.enforcedIn: `RouterRegistry`: `retire` requires the router to have been in SUNSET for at least `RETENTION` ({12 §3}, {12 §13})

rationale.why: In SUNSET a router cannot charge and cannot be the target of a successor, but customers can still revoke, pause and create successors elsewhere ({12 §3}). The reactivation reminders of {12 §11.1} run 30, 60 and 90 days after sunset and a clean-up reminder follows retirement. `RETENTION` keeps the router in that state long enough for those flows and for the support and legal retention needs. 365 days is the proposal of OD-026.
rationale.prevents: Too short: the reactivation and clean-up windows close early and records tied to the router can be retired before support and legal needs end. Too long: the RETIRED state, which marks the end of the router's life and triggers the 'remove leftover permissions' reminder, arrives late, and the data and monitoring kept per router version accumulate (retention rules of PB-030).
rationale.mine: 365 days is the proposal of OD-026, not a decision. My additions: the lower bound equal to PC-01 (customers get at least as long after sunset to recover as they had before it to prepare) and the 730-day hard maximum. The support and legal retention analysis that 16 §7 asks for has not been done.

records.name: MAX_BATCH: maximum entries in one migration-plan step and mandates in one pin batch
records.enforcedIn: `MigrationQueue.step` accepts at most `MAX_BATCH` entries per step (a plan itself has no such bound: it is one word of storage), and `MandateGateway.updateAccountPins` / `updateAccountPinsBySig` at most `MAX_BATCH` mandates ({12 §5.3.1}, {12 §13}, {17 §5.3}, {16 §8.1}, ADR-022)

proposal.unitLabel: count (successors per plan step, or mandates per pin batch)

testnet.text: None: the production value is kept on testnet; the constant is not in {16 §6} ({14 §4.5} rule 1)

rationale.why: One migration plan moves every lineage a customer has on a router; it is executed in steps ({12 §5.3.1}, ADR-022). A step runs the containment check, the exposure-index updates, the Permit2 allowance reads and the event of every entry, so the number of entries per step is what keeps a step inside one transaction. The same constant bounds the number of mandates in one pin update batch.
rationale.prevents: An unbounded loop or a step that cannot be submitted (the customer could not migrate or re-pin), and on the low side a plan that takes so many transactions that siblings stay unfunded between steps in an emergency migration.
rationale.mine: 10 is my proposal after a measurement on the actual contracts (contracts/test/Gas.t.sol, forge 1.8.5, Solidity 0.8.24, cancun schedule, every account and slot cold, entries of three tokens drawn from eight exposed tokens on each router, the old allowances locked down): a worst-case entry costs 545,000 to 605,000 gas and about 4,000 bytes of calldata, so a step of 10 costs about 6.5 million gas in a transaction (execution plus intrinsic and calldata). That is 39% of the 16,777,216 gas per transaction that EIP-7825 sets (an assumption about the launch chains, not verified here) and 78% of the budget the test enforces (half of that cap, to leave room for a chain whose schedule is costlier). The value 50 of OD-026 does not fit: it costs about 30 million gas. The hard range [4, 20] is mine: 4 is the least that keeps MAX_EXPOSED_TOKENS_PER_ROUTER <= MAX_BATCH * MAX_TOKENS_PER_MANDATE (X-06); 20 is the largest step that still fits the cap with a margin. The measurement is on the EVM gas schedule of the compiler's target only: Arbitrum's gas accounting and the real limits of the three chains are not measured (RP-19).

records.name: FEE_CEILING_BPS: immutable ceiling of the fee
records.enforcedIn: `FeeController` (constructor argument stored as an immutable): `setFee` reverts above it; every mandate's `maxFeeBps` must be at most the ceiling ({11 §3}); guard G6 ({11 §4.8}); containment clause K.8 ({12 §5.3.2}); invariant `I-MINOUT`

rationale.mine: No number is proposed here and none appears in this record. The safe range is a rule, not a number: the ceiling must be at most the maximum fee the merchant agreement permits and at least the gas plus operations cost at the lowest supported ticket. The rule was requested for this register; the two quantities it refers to do not exist yet.

records.name: MAX_QUOTE_TTL: immutable ceiling of the life of a price quote
records.enforcedIn: `TokenPolicyRegistry`: `setMaxQuoteTtl` reverts above `MAX_QUOTE_TTL`; the quote verifier checks `validUntil - issuedAt <= min(mandate.maxQuoteAge, registry.maxQuoteTtl)` (Q12) ({11 §4.2}, {11 §4.3}, {16 §8.1})

testnet.text: 30 seconds in a `-testconst` build ({16 §6}): only the speed of the quote tests changes and the TTL check is identical. The testnet `QUOTE_SET_GRACE` (60 s, PC-08) is at least this value, so X-01 holds on the testnet values

rationale.why: A quote attests a price at `issuedAt`; the TTL bounds how long it can be consumed (Q12). The ceiling is immutable so that governance cannot make quotes arbitrarily stale. 300 seconds is two and a half times the default quote TTL of 120 seconds (OD-027, backend-tunable), which leaves room for submission latency and retries, and it is the unit of the rotation grace (PC-08).
rationale.prevents: Stale prices accepted through a depeg (the replay of RP-14) and a longer exposure window for a compromised or mistaken signer (B2, {11 §4.7} KR-5). On the low side, quotes that expire before inclusion, so fiat-capped charges fail closed.
rationale.mine: 300 seconds is the proposal of {16 §7}, not a decision. The hard minimum of 120 seconds (the default TTL must fit), the hard maximum of 600 seconds and the remark about headroom are mine.

records.name: MAX_BAND_WIDTH_BPS: immutable ceiling of the width of a price band
records.enforcedIn: `TokenPolicyRegistry`: `setBounds` reverts if the width of `[minPriceE18, maxPriceE18]` exceeds the ceiling ({11 §4.3}, {16 §8.1}); mandates snapshot the bounds (`I-BOUNDS-SNAPSHOT`)

proposal.unitLabel: basis points (width = ceil(10,000 × (max − min) / min), proposed definition)

testnet.text: None: not listed in {16 §6}; the production value is kept on testnet

rationale.why: The bands are the on-chain limit of what a quote signer can distort: with a malicious signer inside the bounds the outflow is at most `F / m`, where `m` is the lowest in-band price ({11 §6}, B2). The ceiling is immutable so that no governance action can widen a band past a stated blast radius. At the proposal the excess of that bound over the fiat cap is at most about the width of the band, so about 5%. 500 bps is above the roughly ±2% band of OD-027 and ASM-026, so a registry band for a stablecoin has margin and can be widened a little in a stress without a new registry.
rationale.prevents: Too high: a malicious or mistaken signer can mis-price by more than the design intends, and B2 grows with the width. Too low: no registry band can be wide enough for the normal price noise of a candidate stablecoin; honest quotes fail with `PriceOutOfBounds` and fiat-capped charges fail closed.
rationale.mine: 500 bps is the proposal of {16 §7}, not a decision. The definition of 'width' is mine: no document defines it. I propose `ceil(10,000 × (maxPriceE18 − minPriceE18) / minPriceE18)`, measured on the minimum because B2 is stated on the lowest price. Under that definition the ±2% example band (0.98 to 1.02) is 409 bps wide, which is the hard minimum; the hard maximum of 1,000 bps is also mine.

records.name: QUOTE_SET_GRACE: grace for quotes issued before a planned signer-set rotation
records.enforcedIn: `QuoteVerifier` library, check Q13: `block.timestamp <= retiredAt(v) + QUOTE_SET_GRACE` for a quote of a retired signer set `v` ({11 §4.2}, {11 §4.7})

testnet.text: 60 seconds ({16 §6}): at least the testnet `MAX_QUOTE_TTL` of 30 seconds (PC-06), so X-01 holds on the testnet values; it also equals twice that value, the upper edge of X-02

rationale.why: New semantics in 0.5: the grace bounds only the honoring of quotes issued before a planned rotation (`issuedAt < retiredAt(v)` and `now <= retiredAt(v) + QUOTE_SET_GRACE`). A key believed compromised gets no grace: it is tombstoned at once and Q1 fails for it in every set version ({11 §4.7}, KR-4). At a planned rotation the old set is retired at `retiredAt`; quotes already issued under it must stay consumable for as long as a quote can live (`MAX_QUOTE_TTL`), otherwise honest quotes die at every rotation. Hence the range from `MAX_QUOTE_TTL` to twice that.
rationale.prevents: Honest quotes dying at a rotation (grace too short) and, in the other direction, a retired key's quotes and the retired key itself lingering longer than needed (grace too long). The grace never applies to a removed key.
rationale.mine: 300 seconds equals {16 §7} and OD-034 (`QUOTE_SET_GRACE = MAX_QUOTE_TTL = 300 s`); it is not a decision. The range `[MAX_QUOTE_TTL, 2 * MAX_QUOTE_TTL]` is stated in {11 §4.7}. Placing the proposal at the lower edge is mine: it is the shortest grace that kills no honest quote, and no measured need for more exists.

records.name: MAX_SIGNERS_PER_SET: bound of a quote-signer set
records.newIn05Note: **New in 0.5 (implementation evidence).** The implementation of the signer sets needs a bound that no document stated: the members of a set are looped over when a set is proposed and when it is activated (the emergency rotation), and without a bound the gas of the activation that must always succeed is unbounded. Finding F-04 of the implementation report asked for this record; it was written when the contracts were built.
records.enforcedIn: `SignerSetRegistry.proposeSignerSet`: a set has at most `MAX_SIGNERS_PER_SET` members; a larger proposal reverts `TooManySigners` before any loop runs. `verifySigner` (Q1 and Q13) is O(1) whatever the size of a set: it reads the tombstone, the set and the membership flag, never the member list ({11 §4.7}, ADR-023)

testnet.text: None: the production value is kept on testnet; the constant is not in {16 §6}

rationale.why: A quote-signer set is a list of keys. Proposing a set writes each member, and activating it (the emergency rotation after a signer compromise) reads each member to refuse a key that was removed after the proposal. Those two loops are the only loops over members; the check that runs on every charge does not loop. The bound keeps the activation, the one transaction that must always fit in a block, finite.
rationale.prevents: Too high: a proposal that cannot be activated in one block, so an emergency rotation fails exactly when it is needed. Too low: no room for key redundancy (two operators, two regions) and for overlapping old and new members during a planned rotation.
rationale.mine: 16 is my proposal; no document stated a bound. The measurement on the contracts (contracts/test/Registries.t.sol): `verifySigner` costs the same gas for a set of 1, 2, 8 and 16 members (O(1), asserted equal), and proposing and activating a set of 16 stays well inside one block. The hard range [2, 64] is mine: 2 is the least that gives any redundancy; 64 keeps the proposal under about 3 million gas by linear extrapolation of the measurement at 16.

existing.note: a compromised quote signer signs inside the bounds until removed
the grace and the bounds of a rotation (11 §4.7)

evidence.toProduce: Fork gas measurement of the activation at 16 members on each launch chain (RP-19: none yet); the operational size of the quote-signer key set (Risk Lead, Head of Security): none yet.

safeRange.tooLow: A set of one has no redundancy: losing the key halts every fiat-capped charge until an emergency rotation is activated.
safeRange.tooHigh: Proposal and activation grow linearly; a larger set is also a larger attack surface (every member can sign a quote inside the bounds).
safeRange.governance: Governance cannot change it. A different bound is a new `SignerSetRegistry`.
safeRange.position: 16 is 14 above the hard minimum and 48 below the hard maximum: at the low end of the range.
